userHoldings_intro: Not from the original source sheet's ~90x screen — added at the user's specific request for a stock they already hold. Already midcap-sized, so it was not scored against this project's microcap 10x-in-2-3-years framework; presented here as a standalone deleveraging/re-rating scenario analysis instead.

userHoldings.name: Samhi Hotels Ltd
userHoldings.tagline: NSE: SAMHI | Hotel ownership (Marriott/Hyatt/Accor brands), ~Rs 3,700-3,800 Cr — flat for 2 years despite improving fundamentals
userHoldings.summary: User has held this ~2 years with no price movement (52-week range Rs 127-228, currently ~Rs 163-165). Research finding: the stagnation is best explained by a technical overhang — pre-IPO PE investors (Goldman Sachs, GTI, ACIC Mauritius) sold down roughly Rs 900 Cr of stock against a ~Rs 3,700 Cr market cap over 21 months (FII holding fell from 69.5% to ~44.6%), absorbed mostly by retail. Underneath that, the business genuinely improved: net debt/EBITDA down from >6x pre-IPO to ~2.4-3.2x now (management target: 2.5x by FY28), interest cost down ~65%, RevPAR +10% YoY, ~79% occupancy. It also trades at roughly half the peer-average EV/EBITDA (~9-11x vs ~16x for Chalet Hotels/Lemon Tree/EIH/Juniper Hotels) despite comparable or faster EBITDA growth — the ValuePickr thread ('Samhi Hotels - Turnaround with Tailwinds', 20+ pages) frames this gap as the core thesis.
userHoldings.conclusion: Both scenarios rest on a 'deleveraging equity kicker' — EBITDA growth, multiple re-rating, and debt paydown all compounding into the equity simultaneously — which is exactly why the same mechanics would compress returns sharply if EBITDA growth stalls, the remaining ~15% ACIC Mauritius stake hits the market faster than absorbed, or continued capex keeps competing with debt paydown (the ValuePickr community's own bear case). Full detail in the standalone Samhi Hotels doc in this folder. Not scored against this project's microcap framework — this is a follow-up analysis, not a ranked screen result.

methodology_intro: Every stock was scored across the following dimensions, drawing on Screener.in fundamentals, ValuePickr/X sentiment, BSE corporate-action checks, and (where available) technical posture. Market-cap headroom was treated as a hard gate, not just one factor among many — a stock already at midcap-or-larger size cannot plausibly 10x within 2-3 years, so those names were moved to the exclusion list regardless of business quality.
scoring_dimensions: Fundamental momentum (revenue/PAT growth trajectory, margin trend, ROCE/ROE)
Valuation runway (P/E, P/B vs history/sector; room to re-rate without heroic assumptions)
Market-cap headroom (must be genuinely micro/small-cap today)
Catalyst clarity (specific, verifiable near-term triggers vs vague optimism)
Quality/governance screen (promoter holding trend, red flags, regulatory issues)
Liquidity/float (SME-platform or thinly-traded names are flagged, not excluded outright)
Conviction/sentiment signal (weighted lower than hard fundamentals — forum enthusiasm is not proof)
methodology_note: Given the scale of this project (108 names from a compiled ValuePickr/X sheet, researched over one extended session using a token-efficient methodology of targeted web searches rather than exhaustive multi-source deep dives per name), treat this as a well-informed first-pass screen, not exhaustive due diligence on any single name. Before sizing a real position in anything ranked here, do a fresh, current check of the numbers and re-read the underlying ValuePickr thread if one exists.
tierA_intro: Names combining genuine microcap/smallcap size, real (not narrative-only) fundamental momentum, and no material red flags found in this research.

tierA.name: Bansal Roofing Products Ltd
tierA.rationale: Rare combination: ROCE 34%/ROE 28% AND accelerating growth (+27% sales, +32% PAT in Q1 FY27) AND visible, disclosed order wins. Genuine ValuePickr thread exists, tagged 'untested' by the community itself — still early-stage in coverage.

tierA.name: RNIT AI Solutions Ltd
tierA.tagline: Govt-scale facial recognition SaaS, Rs 363-636 Cr
tierA.rationale: Growth claims independently verified against real financials (revenue +59.8%, EBITDA +108.7%, margin to 41.7%) — rare for this dataset. Differentiated moat (3bn+ ID verifications processed for Indian government). Main risk: government-contract concentration.

tierA.name: GPT Healthcare Ltd
tierA.tagline: Eastern India multi-specialty hospitals, Rs 1,281 Cr
tierA.rationale: ROCE/ROE in the high-teens to mid-20s with real above-industry revenue growth (14.25% vs 3.54% industry). Specific, credible operational drivers (occupancy, ARPOB, Raipur ramp) rather than vague optimism. Framed as genuinely under-discovered.

tierA.name: Dynamic Cables Ltd
tierA.rationale: ROCE 26.2%/ROE 19.9%, nearly debt-free, 53.2% 5yr profit CAGR. Source-sheet's specific quarterly claims (+33% revenue, +37% profit) independently corroborated by the broader fundamental data.

tierA.name: Novartis India Ltd
tierA.tagline: ChrysCapital PE buyout special situation, Rs 3,974 Cr
tierA.rationale: The clearest, most specific catalyst in the entire dataset: ChrysCapital took control from Novartis AG in Jul 2026 with a named 'branded generics roll-up' strategy and a credible sponsor track record (Intas, Eris, Corona Remedies). Caveat: stock already +87% since the deal price, so a lot of the initial re-rating has happened — this is a real but partially-played-out special situation, not a fresh discovery.

tierA.name: Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem Ltd
tierA.rationale: Clean earnings-reversal setup: weak 5yr history (11% growth) now being challenged by a genuinely strong, confirmed Q1 FY27 (+43% YoY revenue) and bullish forward analyst estimates (+47.5%/yr earnings). Price has already moved (+62% 1yr) — entry timing matters here.

tierA.name: Repono Ltd
tierA.rationale: ROCE 27.4%/ROE 22.4% with real 29% revenue growth at a cheap P/E (11.7x) — strong fundamentals. Trading below its IPO price, which could be value or could reflect market skepticism not yet understood. SME-platform liquidity is the binding practical constraint.

tierA.name: Antelopus Selan Energy Ltd (formerly Selan Exploration)
tierA.tagline: Oil & gas E&P, Gujarat, Rs 2,755-2,782 Cr
tierA.rationale: Real, accelerating production growth (+14% boepd FY26, higher in Q4) with 7 new wells planned and healthy ROCE/ROE (21.2%/15.9%). One caveat: part of the headline 27% profit growth was an accounting change (reduced amortization), not pure operations — the production trend is the cleaner signal.

tierA.name: Haldyn Glass Ltd
tierA.rationale: Confirmed, significant outperformance (+19.4% YTD vs Sensex -9.7%) independently corroborated by repeated MarketsMojo 'valuation attractiveness' coverage — a rare case of third-party validation beyond just community sentiment.

tierA.name: Asahi Songwon Colors Ltd
tierA.rationale: Real margin-driven profit inflection (PAT roughly 10x sequentially over 2 quarters) at a reasonable valuation (P/B 1.6x), with a decade-long rising promoter-holding trend. Weekly/monthly technicals show a healthy, not overextended, uptrend — potentially earlier-stage than peers.

tierA.name: Macpower CNC Machines Ltd
tierA.rationale: ROCE ~28%, near-zero debt, and a curator thesis that explicitly survived scrutiny 'despite mixed external feedback.' FY25 growth wobble (8.6% vs 24-26% historical) appears to be resolving per independent Q3 FY26 coverage of 'robust growth momentum continuing.'

tierA.name: ADF Foods Ltd
tierA.rationale: ROCE 21.8%/ROE 17.7% with genuine double-digit revenue growth (+25.9%), though profit growth (13.4%) is lagging — a margin gap worth watching as the new Surat plant ramps.

tierB_intro: Real positives in each, but with a specific caveat (liquidity, valuation richness, unproven trend, or slower growth) that keeps conviction moderate rather than high.

tierB.name: Unihealth Hospitals Ltd
tierB.rationale: Strong, consistent growth (30-50%+ across horizons) and high ROCE (24.5%), but SME-platform liquidity and genuine geographic-concentration/verification risk (explicitly raised by the ValuePickr community itself, not just this research).

tierB.name: TPL Plastech Ltd
tierB.tagline: Packaging, Time Technoplast subsidiary, Rs 620 Cr
tierB.rationale: Strong headline growth (+37.6% Q1 revenue) but independent analyst coverage explicitly flags margin erosion beneath it — genuinely unresolved, not a clean story.

tierB.name: Vistar Amar Ltd
tierB.rationale: Cheap (P/E 10x), debt-free, 25.5% ROCE, but highly volatile quarterly margins (-25% to +12.7%) reflecting real commodity exposure.

tierB.name: Devson Catalyst Ltd
tierB.rationale: Strong pre-IPO fundamentals (ROE 43.2%, debt-free) but very short public track record (listed Jul 2026) and SME liquidity.

tierB.name: Fredun Pharmaceuticals Ltd
tierB.rationale: Exceptional growth (90% TTM profit growth) backing the curator's ~90%-portfolio conviction, but negative free cash flow and a 201-day cash-conversion cycle raise a real earnings-quality question beneath the growth headline.

tierB.name: Rapicut Carbides Ltd
tierB.rationale: Genuine tungsten-supercycle tailwind and sharp recent profit inflection, but highly volatile quarterly history and a disclosed related-party transaction concentration with the promoter's other entity.

tierB.name: Bajaj Steel Industries Ltd
tierB.rationale: Excellent ROCE/ROE (27.6%/21.8%) at a real discount to peers, but flat 5yr growth (0.53%) — no visible catalyst to trigger a re-rating.

tierB.name: Fluidomat Ltd
tierB.rationale: Genuinely excellent long-term record (ROCE 30%, debt-free, real moat vs. MNC peer Voith) but currently hitting a real air pocket — TTM profit growth has turned negative and working capital has deteriorated sharply (239 to 411 days).

tierB.name: Capital Small Finance Bank Ltd
tierB.rationale: Real current momentum (22% loan growth, improving NIM), but management's own Vision 2029 target implies only ~2x loan-book growth — a 10x market-cap outcome would need unusually large multiple re-rating on top.

tierB.name: Amrutanjan Health Care Ltd
tierB.rationale: Dominant market position (#1, 41.1% share), debt-free, ROCE 24.8% — but 5yr growth of just 8.6%/yr is a mature-brand profile, not a growth story, without a new catalyst.

tierB.name: Aarti Surfactants Ltd
tierB.rationale: PAT rising sequentially for 3 quarters, promoters added via rights issue, but sits atop a negative 5yr profit trend not yet fully reversed; MarketsMojo flagged margin compression as recently as Q4 FY26.

tierB.name: Trejhara Solutions Ltd
tierB.tagline: Enterprise software, Aurionpro subsidiary, Rs 428 Cr
tierB.rationale: Very fast growth (+70% TTM sales) and a real promoter-stake jump (23% to 34% in one year), but ROE/ROCE both in the low single digits — growth hasn't yet translated into efficient returns. Weekly RSI ~80, very overbought.

tierB.name: Repco Home Finance Ltd
tierB.rationale: Improving ROE trend and 3 consecutive years of rising profit, but weak historical 5yr growth (5.43%) — a slow turnaround, not a demonstrated high-growth story.

tierC_intro: Real elements of a story in each, but either explicitly speculative per the source curator, unconfirmed by independent data, or currently in a documented decline — lower priority.

tierC.name: MV Electrosystems Ltd
tierC.tagline: Railway propulsion electronics, Rs 1,669 Cr (fresh IPO)
tierC.rationale: Large order book (Rs 921.64 Cr, ~18.6x FY26 revenue) but currently loss-making with revenue down 21% YoY — entirely a bet on unproven future execution.

tierC.name: Glen Industries Ltd
tierC.tagline: PLA/paper straws packaging, Rs 274 Cr (BSE SME)
tierC.rationale: Real above-industry growth (22% CAGR) but an independent quality screen explicitly flagged 'weak quality' based on an inconsistent track record — a third-party caution signal, not just this research's view.

tierC.name: Pyramid Technoplast Ltd
tierC.rationale: Real volume growth (20% YoY) with utilization still building, but the source curator himself explicitly flagged this as his most speculative/opportunistic pick.

tierC.name: Gujarat Containers Ltd
tierC.rationale: Cheap (P/E 9.6x) with recent sequential improvement, but sits on a negative 3yr profit trend and worsening working capital; no technical confirmation and no ValuePickr thread found to validate the story.

tierC.name: Unimech Aerospace and Manufacturing Ltd
tierC.rationale: Genuinely strong growth (+71% Q1 revenue) and deep ValuePickr coverage, but already an upper-midcap — included here only because of how strong the underlying story is, not because the size fits a 10x screen.

tierC.name: Go Fashion (India) Ltd
tierC.tagline: Go Colors women's bottomwear, Rs 1,539-2,122 Cr
tierC.rationale: Down -52% over 1 year on a well-documented, multi-quarter margin/demand decline (independently confirmed by repeated MarketsMojo coverage). Latest commentary hints at 'stabilisation' but this is not yet confirmed.

tierC.name: Hi-Tech Gears Ltd
tierC.rationale: Negative growth across nearly every horizon, weak ROCE/ROE, and confirmed active downtrend on both weekly and monthly technicals — a company in decline, not re-rating.

tierC.name: Accel Ltd
tierC.rationale: Statistically cheap (P/E 11.3x, P/B 1.08x) but flat growth, weak returns, meaningful debt relative to size, and confirmed technical weakness — a potential value trap without a specific catalyst.

avoid_intro: Independently corroborated, serious red flags. These are not soft risk factors — treat them as reasons to actively avoid regardless of any price momentum or forum enthusiasm.

avoid.name: Darjeeling Industries
avoid.reason: CONFIRMED active SEBI ex-parte interim order (30 Jun 2026) — MD and 9 others barred from trading over alleged circular funding and stock-price manipulation; company allegedly not found at its registered addresses.

avoid.name: Kerala Ayurveda Ltd
avoid.reason: Severe financial distress: ROE -117.5%, interest coverage just 0.07x (cannot service debt from operations), debt-to-EBITDA >15x, losses widening 19% YoY. Independent media: 'Losses Deepen as Operational Crisis Intensifies.'

avoid.name: Galaxy Supermarket Ltd (Galaxy Cloud Kitchens)
avoid.reason: Negative book value (accumulated losses wiped out all shareholder equity), 3yr/5yr sales CAGR both deeply negative (-11.75%/-25.99%). Two separate independent 'revenue surge masks profitability collapse' warnings across successive quarters.

avoid.name: JITF Infra Logistics Ltd
avoid.reason: Negative consolidated net worth (-Rs 513 Cr), non-current debt over 3x market cap, auditor 'going concern' warnings on two subsidiaries, still consolidated-loss-making despite revenue growth.

avoid.name: AVI Polymers Ltd
avoid.reason: Promoter holding collapsed from 25.19% to 1.10% in a single quarter, alongside a near-zero-to-Rs-312-Cr revenue explosion and extreme ROE (126.5%). Independently downgraded to Sell by MarketsMojo citing valuation concerns.

avoid.name: TechNVision Ventures Ltd
avoid.reason: P/E of 1,161x and ROE of just 1.93% — current earnings do not remotely support the market valuation. Stock already down >50% from its 52-week high.

avoid.name: Alan Scott Enterprises Ltd
avoid.reason: Loss-making every one of the last 4 quarters, ROE -45.8%, negative free cash flow, actively raising capital via rights issue — the strong technical uptrend is disconnected from deeply negative fundamentals.

avoid.name: Samkrg Pistons & Rings Ltd
avoid.reason: Weak 5yr growth (5.2%) and ROE (4.9%), fresh 52-week low, independently rated Sell by MarketsMojo.

avoid.name: High Energy Batteries (India) Ltd
avoid.reason: Sales collapsed quarter-on-quarter (Rs 29.5 Cr to Rs 7.9 Cr), swinging to a loss; flat-to-negative 3-5yr growth despite a P/E of 37.7x.

avoid.name: Vaxfab Enterprises Ltd
avoid.reason: Currently loss-making trading business with very high debtor days (302) despite a +241% 1-year price run well ahead of the fundamentals.
